title: A cheerful face
hookLine: Shammai: receive everyone with a cheerful face (Pirkei Avot 1:15)
tomorrow: Hillel says don't judge someone until you've done what, exactly?

lines: RECEIVE EVERYONE WITH A CHEERFUL FACE.
cards: People who train front-desk staff sometimes say a caller can hear a smile down the phone. The rabbis said something close, and from an unexpected mouth.
Shammai, the sage with a name for strictness, Hillel's rival, has a saying in Pirkei Avot. Make your study a fixed habit. Say little and do much.
And receive every person with a cheerful face. In Hebrew, sever panim yafot. That's the rule about your face.
And it comes from the man at the center of a sharp scene in the Talmud.

teach.b: Here's the scene, from the Talmud. A man who wants to become a Jew comes to Shammai and says: convert me, on one condition. Teach me the whole Torah while I stand on one foot.

Shammai pushes him away with the builder's measuring stick in his hand. The man goes to Hillel, who says: what is hateful to you, don't do to your neighbor. That's the whole Torah; the rest is commentary.
Go and learn it. So the man remembered for pushing someone away is the one who taught the cheerful face. Some teachers read that as a man who knew his own edge and wrote himself the rule he needed.
Either way, the rule stands in Pirkei Avot under his name.

teach.h: THE WELCOME IS PART OF THE GIFT.
teach.b: How you receive a person is part of what you give them. Avot de-Rabbi Natan spells it out: give someone every good gift in the world with a sour face, and Scripture counts it as if you gave nothing.
Receive them with a cheerful face, even with nothing in your hands, and it's as if you gave every good gift. The face isn't decoration. It's the first thing you hand to anyone who walks in.

how: Jews study Shammai's saying in Pirkei Avot, and receiving people with a pleasant face, sever panim yafot, is taught as part of welcoming guests and treating others well.

o: a warm, open welcome for every person who comes
a big grin worn no matter how you feel inside
a calm face that hides every feeling from others

games.q: the strict one and the face: tap the pairs.
p: receive everyone with a cheerful face
what is hateful to you, don't do
wanted the whole Torah at once
a gift with a sour face
counted as if you gave nothing

s: the cheerful-face saying comes from Hillel, the patient one
it's Shammai's, the sage remembered for strictness, in Pirkei Avot 1:15.
the rabbis said a cheerful welcome with empty hands is like giving every good gift
Avot de-Rabbi Natan: with a cheerful face, even giving nothing, it's as if you gave every good gift.

games.q: a neighbor drops by while you're in a foul mood. you can give her the jar of jam she wanted, or just a warm hello. what does Avot de-Rabbi Natan say counts?
o: the warm face; a gift handed over sourly counts as if nothing was given.
the jam; actions count, and the face is only a feeling.
neither; Shammai's rule only covers guests who come to study.
games.why: the welcome is part of the gift. with a cheerful face, even empty hands give something.

practice: Sit comfortably and notice your face from the inside. Let the forehead go smooth, unclench the jaw, let the tongue rest, and soften the skin around the eyes, the place a real welcome starts.
Then hold someone in mind, someone you'll see today, and let your face greet them, gently, as the bell rings.

wordCard.voice: A cheerful face: sever panim yafot, Shammai's rule for how to receive every person who comes to you.

orig.note: Hebrew, Pirkei Avot 1:15: a pleasant, cheerful face, the way to receive every person.

carryVoice: Here's the line: a cheerful face, the gift you can give with empty hands. Day three of the sayings, done.

sources.ref: Pirkei Avot 1:15 (Shammai: make your Torah fixed; say little and do much; receive every person with a cheerful face)
Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 31a (the would-be convert on one foot; Shammai pushes him away with the builder's cubit; Hillel: what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor)
Avot de-Rabbi Natan (A) 13 (on Shammai's saying: gifts given with a downcast face count as nothing; a cheerful face with nothing counts as every good gift)
